security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel writes satp (changing ASID) or hgatp (changing VMID) during context switch or VM enter/exit without a preceding or subsequent fence.hpd instruction, allowing predictor state tagged with the old domain to influence speculation in the new domain. Additionally, ASID or VMID recycling on a CPU without an intervening fence.hpd violates the spec's explicit reuse requirement.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: satp write (csr_write/csr_set/CSR_STATUS/satp=) on context-switch path OR hgatp write on KVM vcpu-load path NOT paired with fence.hpd
security_spec.summary: Context switch and KVM VM enter/exit paths must issue fence.hpd when changing hardware protection domain identifiers (ASID, VMID, SDID) to prevent cross-domain predictor-based transient execution leaks between processes or VMs sharing a physical CPU.

findings.finding: csr_write(CSR_SATP, ...) writes satp with a new ASID during context switch without a preceding or subsequent fence.hpd instruction. If the CPU implements Zihpd/Zifencehpd, hardware predictor state tagged with the old ASID can influence speculation in the new address space, resulting in an info leak across address spaces.

csr_write(CSR_SATP, ...) writes satp during context switch (no-ASID path) without fence.hpd. When changing the page table root, hardware predictor state from the old address space can linger and influence speculation in the new address space.

ASID version rollover: when the ASID space is exhausted, current_version is incremented and all ASIDs are recycled (__flush_context) without any fence.hpd instruction. On CPUs implementing Zihpd, ASID recycling without fence.hpd violates the spec's explicit reuse requirement, allowing predictor state from old-version ASIDs to leak into new-version ASIDs.

ncsr_write(CSR_HGATP, hgatp) writes hgatp with a new VMID during VCPU load (via kvm_arch_vcpu_load at vcpu.c:625) without a fence.hpd instruction. On CPUs implementing Zihpd/Zifencehpd, hardware predictor state tagged with the old VMID can influence speculation in the new guest VM, resulting in cross-VM info leaks.

VMID version rollover and recycling: when vmid_next wraps to zero, vmid_version is incremented and all VMIDs are recycled. The on_each_cpu_mask call does HFENCE_GVMA (TLB flush) but not fence.hpd. On CPUs implementing Zihpd, VMID recycling without fence.hpd violates the spec's reuse requirement, allowing predictor state from old-version VMIDs to leak into new-version VMIDs.

csr_write(CSR_SATP, context->satp) restores satp on resume from suspend. This restores the original satp value (same ASID), but on CPUs implementing Zihpd, even restoring satp may require fence.hpd to clear predictor state that may have been polluted during the suspend period.

The switch_to macro handles FPU, vector, and envcfg switch but does not handle Zihpd/Zifencehpd. This is expected since the kernel has no awareness of these extensions. However, if Zihpd support is added, a fence.hpd would logically fit in or near this sequence.

kvm_arch_vcpu_load writes CSRs including VSATP (line 595/614) as part of guest state restoration, then calls kvm_riscv_mmu_update_hgatp (line 625) which writes HGATP with VMID. Neither satp-related nor hgatp write is paired with fence.hpd. This is the main KVM VM-enter path where hardware predictor state must be cleared.

csr_swap(CSR_HGATP, ...) at line 93 and csr_write(CSR_HGATP, hgatp) at line 107 temporarily change and restore HGATP VMID for TLB shootdown purposes. While the old VMID is restored, the intermediate hgatp write with a different VMID happens without fence.hpd, potentially polluting predictor state.
